cc-bank-yoy-scan.direction: Growth ranges from Bandhan Bank's +523,500.0% down to Bank of Maharashtra's -100.0%, a 523,600.0-point spread.
chain: Bandhan Bank's credit cards grew 523,500.0% YoY, the fastest of 41 banks, ahead of Slice Small Finance Bank's 5,061.7% and DCB Bank's 4,680.6%.

These are small issuers growing off a low base; the largest issuers by card count — HDFC Bank (8.3%), ICICI Bank (8.1%), State Bank of India (7.7%) and Axis Bank (7.3%) — are all growing in single digits.
Bank of Maharashtra sits at the other end, down 100.0% YoY, while RBL Bank is the slowest grower still positive at 2.9%.
cc-bank-yoy-scan.inference: The spread between Bandhan Bank's 523,500.0% and Bank of Maharashtra's -100.0% is wider than last period's 456,600.0-point range, driven almost entirely by small issuers compounding off tiny bases rather than any shift among the largest card issuers, which remain stuck in single-digit growth.

cc-category-allocation.title: Private banks' share of new cards falls to 61.7%, a new low
cc-category-allocation.observation: Private sector banks captured 61.70% of credit cards issued over the trailing 12 months, down from 63.97% last period.
cc-category-allocation.direction: Allocation fell from 63.97% to 61.70% — a 2.26-point drop — now the lowest reading in the 21-month series, below the previous floor of 64.3% set in Jun 2025.
chain: Private sector banks' share of new cards fell to 61.70%, down 2.26 points from 63.97% last period.
The series has now broken below Jun 2025's prior trough of 64.3%, and sits at or near its minimum across the 21-period series.
Allocation has slid from a high of 71.6% in Jan 2025 to 61.70% now, a drop of almost 10 points over 21 months.
cc-category-allocation.inference: At 61.70%, private banks' share of new card issuance is the weakest reading yet in this series, extending a decline that has run almost without interruption since Jan 2025's 71.6%.

cc-category-momentum.title: Private banks add record 1.18 crore cards in 12 months
cc-category-momentum.observation: Private sector banks added 11,808,141 (1.18 crore) credit cards over the trailing 12 months, up from 11,557,952 (1.16 crore) last period.
cc-category-momentum.direction: Momentum rose from 1.16 crore (11,557,952) to 1.18 crore (11,808,141) cards — a 2.50 lakh (250,189) gain — the highest level in the 21-period series.
chain: Private sector banks added 11,808,141 cards (1.18 crore) in the trailing 12 months, up 250,189 (2.50 lakh) from 11,557,952 (1.16 crore) last period.
This is the highest reading in the 21-period series, continuing an almost unbroken climb from 9,372,927 (93.73 lakh) in Jan 2025.
The current 11,808,141 is up from a 2025 low of 7,156,475 in Jun 2025, a gain of 4,651,666 (46.52 lakh) cards added per year.
cc-category-momentum.inference: Private banks' card additions have risen every month since Jan 2026 (7,779,223 then, to 11,808,141 now) and are currently 46.52 lakh above Jun 2025's low of 7,156,475 — the steadiest build in this dataset's history.

cc-category-rotation.title: Small Finance Banks gain 1.06 points of card share in 12 months
cc-category-rotation.observation: Small Finance Banks gained 1.06 points of credit-card share over the trailing 12 months, the largest move of 5 categories.
cc-category-rotation.direction: Small Finance Banks' share rose 1.06 points while Private Sector Banks fell 0.52 points and Foreign Banks fell 0.66 points, a 1.71-point spread between the biggest gainer and biggest loser.
chain: Small Finance Banks gained 1.06 points of credit-card share over 12 months, the only category move large enough to read as strengthening.

Public Sector Banks (+0.12) and Payment Banks (+0.00) moved within a point and read as stable; Private Sector Banks (-0.52) and Foreign Banks (-0.66) both lost more than half a point and read as weakening.
The spread between the top gainer and biggest loser is 1.71 points, with 1.18 points of the category mix rotating in total.
cc-category-rotation.inference: Small Finance Banks are the only category gaining real share (1.06 points) in a mix otherwise splitting between two large categories losing ground — Private Sector Banks down 0.52 points and Foreign Banks down 0.66 points.

cc-category-share-scan.title: Private banks hold 70.4% of credit cards; gap to public banks narrows
cc-category-share-scan.observation: Private sector banks hold 70.4% of all credit cards outstanding, followed by public sector banks at 24.1% and foreign banks at 3.3%.
cc-category-share-scan.direction: The gap between private banks (70.4%) and public sector banks (24.1%) narrowed to 46.3 points, continuing from 46.5 points last period.
chain: Private sector banks hold 70.4% of all credit cards, well ahead of public sector banks at 24.1%, foreign banks at 3.3%, small finance banks at 2.1% and payment banks at 0.0%.
The private-public gap has narrowed to 46.3 points from 46.5 points last period, continuing a run of narrowing readings.
Small finance and payment banks together hold 2.1% of cards, continuing to climb from 2.0% last period.
cc-category-share-scan.inference: The private-public gap keeps narrowing — now 46.3 points, down from 46.5, 46.8 and 46.9 points over the last three readings — while small finance and payment banks' 2.1% combined share is the one segment still gaining ground outside the top two categories.

cc-category-size-scan.title: Credit cards outstanding hit 12.53 crore, a new high
cc-category-size-scan.observation: Credit cards outstanding reached 125,315,381 (12.53 crore) in Sep 2026, up from 124,053,544 (12.41 crore) in Aug 2026.
cc-category-size-scan.direction: The count rose from 12.41 crore to 12.53 crore, adding 12.62 lakh (1,261,837) cards, and now sits at or near the maximum of the 33-period series.
chain: Credit cards outstanding rose to 125,315,381 (12.53 crore) in Sep 2026, up 1,261,837 (12.62 lakh) from 124,053,544 (12.41 crore) in Aug 2026.
This addition is slightly higher than Aug 2026's own gain of 1,195,650 cards, continuing an uninterrupted monthly build.
The count has grown from 99,500,257 (9.95 crore) in Jan 2024 to 125,315,381 (12.53 crore) now, and sits at or near the maximum of the 33-period series.
cc-category-size-scan.inference: The steady, uninterrupted monthly build from 9.95 crore in Jan 2024 to 12.53 crore now is the notable fact here — Sep 2026's addition of 12.62 lakh cards keeps the count at its highest level in the dataset.

cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-allocation.title: HDFC drives +17.2% of value shift; ICICI pulls -28.7%
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-allocation.observation: HDFC Bank accounts for 17.2% of the net movement in credit card eCommerce transaction value, the largest positive share among 40 active banks.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-allocation.direction: ICICI Bank's share of the movement is -28.7%, State Bank of India's is -24.4% and Axis Bank's is -12.8% — all three negative — while HDFC Bank's +17.2% is the only large positive share.
chain: HDFC Bank holds 17.2% of the market's movement in credit card eCommerce transaction value, the top share among 40 active banks.
ICICI Bank (-28.7%), State Bank of India (-24.4%) and Axis Bank (-12.8%) are the three largest negative shares, pulling the overall movement down.
The spread between HDFC's +17.2% and ICICI's -28.7% is 45.8 points, and 28.69% of the entire mix is in motion.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-allocation.inference: The movement in credit card eCommerce value is concentrated in just four banks — HDFC pulling up while ICICI, SBI and Axis pull down — rather than spread evenly across the market.

cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-momentum.title: HDFC adds ₹6,045.4 Cr in card value; ICICI loses ₹10,110.4 Cr
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-momentum.observation: HDFC Bank added ₹6,045.4 Cr in credit card eCommerce transaction value over the past 12 months, the largest gain among 40 banks.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-momentum.direction: ICICI Bank lost ₹10,110.4 Cr over the same 12 months, State Bank of India lost ₹8,595.2 Cr and Axis Bank lost ₹4,525.6 Cr — all three down while HDFC rose.
chain: HDFC Bank's credit card eCommerce transaction value rose by ₹6,045.4 Cr over 12 months, the single largest addition in the table.
ICICI Bank lost ₹10,110.4 Cr and State Bank of India lost ₹8,595.2 Cr over the same period, together erasing nearly three times what HDFC added.
The spread between HDFC's +₹6,045.4 Cr and ICICI's -₹10,110.4 Cr is ₹16,155.8 Cr, with 22 of 40 banks strengthening and 18 weakening.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-momentum.inference: ICICI Bank's ₹10,110.4 Cr decline is the single largest move in either direction in this table, bigger than HDFC's ₹6,045.4 Cr gain — value is shifting away from ICICI faster than it is growing anywhere else.

cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-scan.title: HDFC's card eCommerce value hits ₹44,508.4 Cr, over double ICICI
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-scan.observation: HDFC Bank recorded ₹44,508.4 Cr in credit card eCommerce transaction value, the highest of 63 banks and more than double ICICI Bank's ₹22,046.0 Cr.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-scan.direction: HDFC Bank (₹44,508.4 Cr, strengthening) leads; ICICI Bank (₹22,046.0 Cr) and State Bank of India (₹20,633.4 Cr) rank second and third but are both weakening, as is Axis Bank (₹11,098.2 Cr) in fourth.
chain: HDFC Bank's ₹44,508.4 Cr in credit card eCommerce value is the largest in the table of 63 banks.
ICICI Bank (₹22,046.0 Cr), State Bank of India (₹20,633.4 Cr) and Axis Bank (₹11,098.2 Cr) are the next three largest, and all three are weakening.
Five banks changed status this period, including Axis Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank and Canara Bank moving from strengthening to weakening, while RBL Bank moved from weakening to strengthening.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-scan.inference: HDFC is strengthening at ₹44,508.4 Cr while ICICI (₹22,046.0 Cr), SBI (₹20,633.4 Cr) and Axis (₹11,098.2 Cr) — the next three largest issuers by value — are all weakening, consistent with the prior period's pattern of HDFC pulling further ahead.

cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-step.title: HDFC's eCommerce value share breaks +3.13 points in one step
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-step.observation: HDFC Bank's share of credit card eCommerce transaction value moved by 3.13 points in a single step, the one break flagged in this table.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-step.direction: HDFC Bank's share step is +3.13 points and strengthening, with no other bank registering a break this period.
chain: HDFC Bank's share of credit card eCommerce transaction value shifted by 3.13 points in a step rather than a gradual move.
No other bank among those tracked shows a step break this period — HDFC is the only one flagged.
This sits alongside HDFC's position as the largest and strengthening entity in both the value level and allocation tables.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-step.inference: A 3.13-point step in HDFC's share, rather than a gradual climb, is a one-period jump distinct from the steady gains showing up elsewhere in HDFC's value trajectory.

cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-yoy-scan.title: Slice SFB's card value up 3,126.8% YoY, fastest of 39 banks
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-yoy-scan.observation: Slice Small Finance Bank's credit card eCommerce transaction value grew 3,126.8% year-on-year, the fastest of 39 active banks.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-yoy-scan.direction: Slice Small Finance Bank's YoY growth accelerated from 2,798.2% last period to 3,126.8% now, still the fastest in the table and well ahead of DCB Bank's 812.2%; the steepest decline eased from Bank of Maharashtra's -100.0% last period to South Indian Bank's -40.8% now.
chain: Slice Small Finance Bank's credit card eCommerce transaction value rose 3,126.8% year-on-year, ahead of DCB Bank's 812.2% and Equitas Small Finance Bank's 443.1%.
HDFC Bank, the largest issuer by value, grew a comparatively modest 15.7% YoY, while ICICI Bank (-31.4%), State Bank of India (-29.4%) and Axis Bank (-29.0%) all contracted.
The spread from Slice's +3,126.8% to South Indian Bank's -40.8% is 3,167.6 points, spanning entrants growing off a small base and large incumbents in decline.
cc-ecom-txn-val-bank-yoy-scan.inference: Slice Small Finance Bank's growth kept accelerating even as last period's worst decliner, Bank of Maharashtra at -100.0%, no longer anchors the bottom — South Indian Bank's -40.8% is a far shallower low — while three of the largest incumbents, ICICI (-31.4%), SBI (-29.4%) and Axis (-29.0%), are still contracting by roughly similar amounts.

cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-allocation.title: SBI drives 34.6% of card volume's movement, the largest share
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-allocation.observation: State Bank of India accounts for 34.6% of the net movement in credit card eCommerce transaction volume, the largest share of any bank.
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-allocation.direction: ICICI Bank's share of the movement is 17.4% and Federal Bank's is 9.6%, both positive like SBI's 34.6%, while Axis Bank is the only large negative share at -6.2%.
chain: State Bank of India holds 34.6% of the market's movement in credit card eCommerce transaction volume, well ahead of ICICI Bank's 17.4% and Federal Bank's 9.6%.
Axis Bank's share of the movement is -6.2%, the only sizable negative figure among 40 active banks.
The spread between SBI's +34.6% and Axis Bank's -6.2% is 40.8 points, with 34.64% of the entire mix in motion.
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-allocation.inference: Unlike the value-based movement where ICICI, SBI and Axis all pull down, in volume terms SBI (34.6%), ICICI (17.4%) and Federal Bank (9.6%) are all driving the movement up together, with Axis Bank the lone large decliner.

cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-momentum.title: SBI adds 2.25 crore card eCommerce transactions in 12 months
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-momentum.observation: State Bank of India added 2.25 crore credit card eCommerce transactions over the past 12 months, the largest increase among 40 banks.
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-momentum.direction: ICICI Bank added 1.13 crore transactions and HDFC Bank added 18.50 lakh over the same period, while Axis Bank lost 40.25 lakh transactions, the only large decline.
chain: State Bank of India's credit card eCommerce transaction volume rose by 2.25 crore transactions over 12 months, the single largest addition in the table.
ICICI Bank added 1.13 crore and HDFC Bank added 18.50 lakh over the same period — all three of the largest issuers gained volume.
Axis Bank lost 40.25 lakh transactions, the only sizable decline among 30 strengthening and 10 weakening banks; the spread between SBI's +2.25 crore and Axis's -40.25 lakh is 2.65 crore.
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-momentum.inference: Volume growth in credit card eCommerce is broad-based — SBI, ICICI and HDFC, the three largest issuers, are all adding transactions together, with Axis Bank the only major bank losing volume.

cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-scan.title: SBI's card eCommerce volume hits 8.57 crore, narrowly tops ICICI
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-scan.observation: State Bank of India recorded 8.57 crore credit card eCommerce transactions, the highest of 63 banks and narrowly ahead of ICICI Bank's 8.25 crore.
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-scan.direction: SBI (8.57 crore, strengthening) leads just ahead of ICICI Bank (8.25 crore, strengthening); HDFC Bank's 4.17 crore is less than half SBI's volume and also strengthening, while Axis Bank's 2.81 crore in fourth is weakening.
chain: State Bank of India's 8.57 crore credit card eCommerce transactions is the highest in the table of 63 banks, narrowly ahead of ICICI Bank's 8.25 crore.
HDFC Bank's 4.17 crore trails both, while Axis Bank's 2.81 crore in fourth place is weakening, unlike the top three.
Axis Bank and Indian Bank both shifted from strengthening to weakening this period, while Bank of Maharashtra moved from weakening to active.
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-scan.inference: Axis Bank has flipped from strengthening last period to weakening now, breaking what had been four largest issuers — SBI, ICICI, HDFC and Axis — all gaining in volume together; the top three, SBI (8.57 crore), ICICI (8.25 crore) and HDFC (4.17 crore), continue to strengthen.

cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-yoy-scan.title: Slice Small Finance Bank's card eCom volume surges 7340.2% YoY
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-yoy-scan.observation: Slice Small Finance Bank's credit card eCommerce transaction volume grew 7340.2% year-on-year, the fastest among 39 banks tracked.
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-yoy-scan.direction: Slice's 7340.2% growth is more than 3x DCB Bank's 2068.7% and well ahead of Punjab National Bank's 1645.1%, while SBM Bank India posted the weakest reading at -18.6%.
chain: Slice Small Finance Bank's eCommerce transaction volume grew 7340.2% YoY, the fastest of 39 banks, ahead of DCB Bank's 2068.7% and Punjab National Bank's 1645.1%.
The gap between Slice's growth and the weakest reading, SBM Bank India's -18.6%, is 7358.8 points.

Seven banks — Slice, DCB, Punjab National Bank, Bank of India (907.9%), Suryoday Small Finance Bank (363.4%), Equitas Small Finance Bank (340.4%) and Federal Bank (316.2%) — grew more than 300%, while 10 of the 39 banks show negative YoY growth.
cc-ecom-txn-vol-bank-yoy-scan.inference: With Slice Small Finance Bank up 7340.2% against a 7358.8-point spread and 10 of 39 banks in negative territory, growth in card eCommerce volume continues to concentrate in a small set of low-base issuers rather than spreading across the banking system.

cc-issuance-vs-spend-bank-gap.title: ICICI Bank's card issuance outpaces spend by 34.38pp, widest gap
cc-issuance-vs-spend-bank-gap.observation: ICICI Bank is issuing credit cards 34.38 points faster year-on-year than its cards are being spent on, the widest gap among the 4 active banks in this cut.
cc-issuance-vs-spend-bank-gap.direction: ICICI's gap widened sharply from +15.36pp last period to +34.38pp now, while State Bank of India (+21.84pp) and Axis Bank (+18.43pp) are newly active in this cut; CSB Bank's gap narrowed slightly to +15.23pp from +17.98pp.
chain: ICICI Bank's issuance-vs-spend gap is +34.38pp, the widest of 4 banks now tracked, ahead of State Bank of India at +21.84pp and Axis Bank at +18.43pp.
CSB Bank, the smallest gap in this cut, stands at +15.23pp.
The spread across the 4 banks is +19.14pp, from ICICI's +34.38pp down to CSB Bank's +15.23pp — card issuance is outrunning card spend at every bank in this cut, not just one.
cc-issuance-vs-spend-bank-gap.inference: All 4 banks tracked here show cards being issued faster than they are spent on, with ICICI Bank's +34.38pp gap now more than double CSB Bank's +15.23pp — the issuance-ahead-of-spend pattern has broadened beyond the single bank seen last period.

cc-issuance-vs-spend-gap.title: Card issuance-vs-spend gap jumps to 16.3pp, highest in 21 periods
cc-issuance-vs-spend-gap.observation: Credit cards are being issued 16.3 points faster year-on-year than they are being spent on in Sep 2026, the highest reading in the 21-period dataset.
cc-issuance-vs-spend-gap.direction: The gap widened to 16.3pp from 4.4pp last period (Aug 2026) — an 11.9 point jump — extending the climb from -0.4pp in Jun 2026 → 2.5pp in Jul 2026 → 4.4pp in Aug 2026 → 16.3pp in Sep 2026.
chain: The issuance-vs-spend gap reached 16.3pp in Sep 2026, up from 4.4pp in Aug 2026 — an 11.9 point increase in a single period.
This is the third straight period the gap has stayed positive, climbing from 2.5pp in Jul 2026 through 4.4pp in Aug 2026 to 16.3pp now, a reversal from -0.4pp as recently as Jun 2026.
At 16.3pp, the gap sits at or near the maximum of the 21-period history, meaning card issuance has rarely if ever outpaced card spend by this much before.
cc-issuance-vs-spend-gap.inference: The gap has nearly quadrupled in one period (4.4pp → 16.3pp) and now sits at the high end of 21 periods of data, its third straight positive reading after turning positive again in Jul 2026 following a negative Jun 2026 (-0.4pp).

cc-other-txn-val-bank-allocation.title: Utkarsh SFB captures 89.9% of card 'other' value's rotation

chain: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank holds 89.9% of the shift in credit card 'other' transactions value, against DCB Bank's 10.3%.
Punjab National Bank sits at 0.0%, AU Small Finance Bank at -0.0% and ICICI Bank at -0.1% — negligible movement.
The rotation mass — the share of the mix that moved — is 89.62pp, meaning almost all the reshuffling in this category sits with Utkarsh and DCB Bank alone.
cc-other-txn-val-bank-allocation.inference: With a rotation mass of 89.62pp split almost entirely between Utkarsh Small Finance Bank (89.9%) and DCB Bank (10.3%), movement in credit card 'other' transactions value is concentrated in just two of the 10 tracked banks.

cc-other-txn-val-bank-momentum.title: Utkarsh SFB adds ₹59.99 crore in card 'other' value over 12 months
cc-other-txn-val-bank-momentum.observation: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank added ₹59.99 crore in credit card 'other' transactions value over the past 12 months, the largest gain among the 5 banks in this cut.
cc-other-txn-val-bank-momentum.direction: Utkarsh's ₹59.99 crore gain is well ahead of DCB Bank's ₹6.85 crore and Punjab National Bank's ₹0.75 lakh, while AU Small Finance Bank lost ₹0.70 lakh and ICICI Bank lost ₹8.63 lakh over the same period.
chain: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank added ₹59.99 crore in 'other' transactions value over 12 months, against DCB Bank's ₹6.85 crore and Punjab National Bank's ₹0.75 lakh.
AU Small Finance Bank (-₹0.70 lakh) and ICICI Bank (-₹8.63 lakh) both lost value over the same 12 months, the only two of 5 banks weakening.
Punjab National Bank's status flipped from weakening to strengthening, while ICICI Bank's flipped from strengthening to weakening — a reversal in direction for both.

cc-other-txn-val-bank-scan.title: Utkarsh SFB's card 'other' value eases to ₹104.52 crore, still leads
cc-other-txn-val-bank-scan.observation: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank recorded ₹104.52 crore in credit card 'other' transactions value, the highest of 63 banks tracked, while 58 of 63 banks show zero.

chain: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank's 'other' transactions value is ₹104.52 crore, the highest of 63 banks, though down from ₹108.32 crore last period.
DCB Bank (₹6.85 crore) and Punjab National Bank (₹2.46 lakh) are the only other active gainers of size, with 58 of 63 banks still at zero.

cc-other-txn-val-bank-step.title: DCB Bank's card 'other' value share rises 1.82pp as Utkarsh falls
cc-other-txn-val-bank-step.observation: DCB Bank's share of credit card 'other' transactions value stepped up 1.82 points, while Utkarsh Small Finance Bank's share stepped down 1.88 points.

cc-other-txn-val-bank-yoy-scan.title: PNB's card 'other' value swings to +44.1%, ICICI reverses to -11.5%
cc-other-txn-val-bank-yoy-scan.observation: Punjab National Bank's credit card 'other' transactions value grew 44.1% year-on-year, while ICICI Bank's fell -11.5% — both reversing direction from last period.

chain: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank leads this cut at 134.7% YoY growth, down from 207.8% last period but still the fastest of the 4 banks.
Punjab National Bank reversed from -35.6% to +44.1%, and ICICI Bank reversed the other way, from +141.4% to -11.5%.

cc-other-txn-vol-bank-allocation.title: Utkarsh SFB took 93.2% of 'other' transaction volume shift
cc-other-txn-vol-bank-allocation.observation: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank accounted for 93.2% of the net movement in credit card 'other' transaction volume, with DCB Bank taking the remaining 6.8%.
cc-other-txn-vol-bank-allocation.direction: Of the market's shifting mix, Utkarsh Small Finance Bank absorbed 93.2% and DCB Bank 6.8%, while Punjab National Bank, ICICI Bank and AU Small Finance Bank each sat near 0.0%.
chain: Utkarsh Small Finance Bank holds 93.2% of the movement in this category, with DCB Bank next at 6.8%.
